annotations.author: Liam Carvajal
annotations.description:
Detects the zone firewall dropping industrial protocol traffic that
originates in the enterprise zone and targets the control zone. A healthy
Purdue segmentation allows no direct path from Level 4/5 to Level 1; traffic
that reaches the firewall boundary is evidence of a misconfigured asset, a
misrouted pivot, or an attempt to reach controllers directly.

The firewall allows the enterprise zone to reach only the industrial DMZ and
the operations zone, so every drop of this shape is a policy violation rather
than routine noise.
annotations.summary: Industrial Protocol Traffic From Enterprise To Control Zone

annotations.author: Liam Carvajal
annotations.description:
Detects a command that is protocol-valid and issued from an authorized
writer, but that violates the physical safety envelope of the process, for
example opening an inlet valve while the tank is full. IP allowlisting and
protocol validation cannot catch this class of event because every individual
field is legitimate.

The physics-aware monitor maintains a shadow of the process state and emits a
structured violation event; this rule classifies it, assigns severity and
routes it for response. It is the safety-layer counterpart to the protocol
detections in this repository.
annotations.summary: Process Safety Violation From Physics-Aware Monitor

annotations.author: Liam Carvajal
annotations.description:
Detects the DNP3 Disable Unsolicited function. Outstations report events
without polling through unsolicited responses; disabling them suppresses that
reporting and can be used to blind operators to process changes.

The function is legitimate during some maintenance procedures, so this rule
should be correlated with a change window before escalation.

annotations.author: Liam Carvajal
annotations.description:
Detects a DNP3 control operation (Select, Operate, Direct Operate or Direct
Operate No Ack) issued by a master that is not an approved control master.
DNP3 control functions change physical outputs, so a control operation from an
unexpected link address is either a compromised host or an unauthorized
engineering change.

The rule operates on decoded DNP3 events (see docs/TELEMETRY.md) produced by
tools/dnp3-dpi. Authorized master link addresses are site-specific.
annotations.summary: DNP3 Control Operation From Unauthorized Master

annotations.author: Liam Carvajal
annotations.description:
Detects a DNP3 Cold Restart or Warm Restart function. Both disrupt an
outstation: a cold restart reinitializes the device, while a warm restart
restarts the application. Outside a maintenance window this is a strong
indicator of an attempt to disrupt control or to force a device into a
recoverable state.
annotations.summary: DNP3 Cold Or Warm Restart Command

annotations.author: Liam Carvajal
annotations.description:

space to enumerate nodes, which is how an attacker discovers the tags and
structures of a controller before acting on them.

Operates on decoded OPC UA events (see docs/TELEMETRY.md) produced by
tools/opcua-dpi. Only plaintext (None/Sign) channels expose the service, so
this rule does not see SignAndEncrypt traffic.

Detects a DNP3 control operation (Select, Operate, Direct Operate or Direct
Operate No Ack) issued by a master that is not an approved control master.
DNP3 control functions change physical outputs, so a control operation from an
unexpected link address is either a compromised host or an unauthorized
engineering change.

The rule operates on decoded DNP3 events (see docs/TELEMETRY.md) produced by
tools/dnp3-dpi. Authorized master link addresses are site-specific.
annotations.summary: DNP3 Control Operation From Unauthorized Master

annotations.author: Liam Carvajal
annotations.description:
Detects a DNP3 Cold Restart or Warm Restart function. Both disrupt an
outstation: a cold restart reinitializes the device, while a warm restart
restarts the application. Outside a maintenance window this is a strong
indicator of an attempt to disrupt control or to force a device into a
recoverable state.
annotations.summary: DNP3 Cold Or Warm Restart Command

annotations.author: Liam Carvajal
annotations.description:
Detects an OPC UA CallRequest, which invokes a method on the server. Methods
can start processes, change configuration or run vendor routines, so a call
from an unexpected client is execution through the OPC UA API.

Operates on decoded OPC UA events (see docs/TELEMETRY.md) produced by
tools/opcua-dpi. Only plaintext (None/Sign) channels expose the service, so
this rule does not see SignAndEncrypt traffic.

annotations.author: Liam Carvajal
annotations.description:
Detects an OPC UA Browse or BrowseNext request. Browsing walks the address
space to enumerate nodes, which is how an attacker discovers the tags and
structures of a controller before acting on them.

Operates on decoded OPC UA events (see docs/TELEMETRY.md) produced by
tools/opcua-dpi. Only plaintext (None/Sign) channels expose the service, so
this rule does not see SignAndEncrypt traffic.

annotations.author: Liam Carvajal
annotations.description:
Detects an OPC UA WriteRequest. Writing node values over OPC UA changes the
data the control system acts on; a write from an unexpected client is either a
compromised host or an unauthorized engineering change.

Operates on decoded OPC UA events (see docs/TELEMETRY.md) produced by
tools/opcua-dpi. Only plaintext (None/Sign) channels expose the service, so
this rule does not see SignAndEncrypt traffic.
A protocol-valid command would violate the physical safety logic of the process.
A Modbus write (FC 6/16) from a non-authorized source was detected on the control network.
A source exceeded the exception-rate threshold, indicating register scanning or brute-forcing.
Multiple direct IT-to-Control communications observed, bypassing the OT conduits.

annotations.author: Liam Carvajal
annotations.description:
Detects the zone firewall dropping industrial protocol traffic that
originates in the enterprise zone and targets the control zone. A healthy
Purdue segmentation allows no direct path from Level 4/5 to Level 1; traffic
that reaches the firewall boundary is evidence of a misconfigured asset, a
misrouted pivot, or an attempt to reach controllers directly.

The firewall allows the enterprise zone to reach only the industrial DMZ and
the operations zone, so every drop of this shape is a policy violation rather
than routine noise.
annotations.summary: Industrial Protocol Traffic From Enterprise To Control Zone

annotations.description: A protocol-valid command would violate the physical safety logic of the process.
A Modbus write (FC 6/16) from a non-authorized source was detected on the control network.

annotations.author: Liam Carvajal
annotations.description:
Detects a command that is protocol-valid and issued from an authorized
writer, but that violates the physical safety envelope of the process, for
example opening an inlet valve while the tank is full. IP allowlisting and
protocol validation cannot catch this class of event because every individual
field is legitimate.

The physics-aware monitor maintains a shadow of the process state and emits a
structured violation event; this rule classifies it, assigns severity and
routes it for response. It is the safety-layer counterpart to the protocol
detections in this repository.
annotations.summary: Process Safety Violation From Physics-Aware Monitor

annotations.description: A Modbus write (FC 6/16) from a non-authorized source was detected on the control network.
A protocol-valid command would violate the physical safety logic of the process.

annotations.author: Liam Carvajal
annotations.description:

reporting and can be used to blind operators to process changes.

The function is legitimate during some maintenance procedures, so this rule
should be correlated with a change window before escalation.

annotations.author: Liam Carvajal
annotations.description:
Detects command-and-control beaconing from an OT host: repeated egress attempts to the same enterprise/external address at a near-constant interval. There is no OT -> Enterprise conduit in a correctly segmented Purdue network, so every attempt is denied by the zone firewall - but the *pattern* of the drops, not the individual drops, is the beacon.

The gateway's firewall-events producer times the denied flows per source and destination and flags them when the interval coefficient of variation is low (regular callbacks). This is a stateful/behavioural detection.
